name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A self-propelled vehicle used for recreation or cross-country travel on public lands, trails, easements, lakes, rivers or streams, motorcycles included; a motorcycle designed for off-road recreation is one unless it's modified to meet highway equipment standards and registered for the road.

restrictions.rule: Includes motorcycles, quadricycles and any other land vehicle powered by something other than muscle or wind; no limit on motor power or speed (Montana Code Annotated §§23-2-801, 61-1-101(50))
Displays a decal from the county treasurer, proof its registration fee is paid, to ride for off-road recreation on public lands
A nonresident's needs a nonresident temporary-use permit sticker instead
A licensed motorcycle used for fishing and hiking access, camping or picnicking on a two-track trail or road within a mile of a designated road needs no decal
May cross a public road directly, at a right angle after a full stop, but never on or across an interstate highway

On a city street, county road or highway only with the permission of the city, county or highway patrol, and on a controlled-access highway only if registered for the road and ridden by a licensed driver
On a public road where allowed, the rider needs a driver's license, unless 12 to 15 with a Fish, Wildlife and Parks off-highway vehicle safety course certificate and a licensed driver present
A rider under 12 may ride a motorcycle on unpaved roads only accompanied by an adult, and must wear a helmet
May use forest development roads the Forest Service designates for off-highway vehicles
